title: The Search for the Wicked Witch, part 8
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Come with me; and see that you mind everything I tell you, for if you do not I will make an end of you, as I did of the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow.”

Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle until they came to the kitchen, where the Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.
Dorothy went to work meekly, with her mind made up to work as hard as she could; for she was glad the Wicked Witch had decided not to kill her.

With Dorothy hard at work, the Witch thought she would go into the courtyard and harness the Cowardly Lion like a horse; it would amuse her, she was sure, to make him draw her chariot whenever she wished to go to drive. But as she opened the gate the Lion gave a loud roar and bounded at her so fiercely that the Witch was afraid, and ran out and shut the gate again.
“If I cannot harness you,” said the Witch to the Lion, speaking through the bars of the gate, “I can starve you. You shall have nothing to eat until you do as I wish.”
So after that she took no food to the imprisoned Lion; but every day she came to the gate at noon and asked, “Are you ready to be harnessed like a horse?”
And the Lion would answer, “No. If you come in this yard, I will bite you.”

The reason the Lion did not have to do as the Witch wished was that every night, while the woman was asleep, Dorothy carried him food from the cupboard. After he had eaten he would lie down on his bed of straw, and Dorothy would lie beside him and put her head on his soft, shaggy mane, while they talked of their troubles and tried to plan some way to escape. But they could find no way to get out of the castle, for it was constantly guarded by the yellow Winkies, who were the slaves of the Wicked Witch and too afraid of her not to do as she told them.

The girl had to work hard during the day, and often the Witch threatened to beat her with the same old umbrella she always carried in her hand. But, in truth, she did not dare to strike Dorothy, because of the mark upon her forehead. The child did not know this, and was full of fear for herself and Toto. Once the Witch struck Toto a blow with her umbrella and the brave little dog flew at her and bit her leg in return. The Witch did not bleed where she was bitten, for she was so wicked that the blood in her had dried up many years before.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what work was Dorothy set to do?
options: Clean the pots, sweep the floor, and feed the fire
Card and spin wool for the Winkies
Carry water from the well each morning
Mind the Witch's wolves and crows

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Witch threaten the Lion with?
options: Starving him until he agreed to be harnessed
Selling him to the Winkies for work
Setting the Winged Monkeys on him
Beating him with her umbrella

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion answer her each noon?
options: That he would bite her if she came into the yard
That he would agree if she fed him first
That he was too weak to answer at all
That he would draw her chariot willingly

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who guarded the castle?
options: The yellow Winkies
The Winged Monkeys
A pack of great wolves
Nobody at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened when the Witch struck Toto?
options: He flew at her and bit her leg
He ran away and hid in the kitchen
He barked but did not move
He was carried off by the Winkies

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the Lion keep from giving in?
options: Dorothy brought him food from the cupboard at night
The Winkies secretly fed him when the Witch slept
He caught rats and mice in the little yard
He went without food and grew weaker

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch never actually strike Dorothy?
options: She did not dare, because of the mark on her forehead
The Winkies would not have allowed it
Dorothy always worked hard enough to please her
She was saving her anger for the Lion

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch not bleed when bitten?
options: She was so wicked her blood had dried up years before
Toto's teeth could not pierce her skin
She was not made of flesh at all
The bite was through her heavy skirts

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does meekly describe about Dorothy's working?
options: Quietly and without complaint
Slowly and unwillingly
Cheerfully and singing
Carelessly and badly

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A captivity in which both prisoners quietly refuse to be broken
A captivity that Dorothy escapes within a few days
A Witch who treats her prisoners kindly after all
A Lion who agrees to draw the Witch's chariot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Witch threaten Dorothy with at first?
options: Making an end of her as she had of the others
Locking her in the yard with the Lion
Setting the Winkies to watch her day and night
Taking away the Silver Shoes

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Witch always carry in her hand?
options: An old umbrella
A silver whistle
A strap for beating
The Golden Cap

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion lie on in the yard?
options: A bed of straw
The bare stones
A heap of old sacks
Dorothy's white dress

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was Dorothy glad to work hard?
options: Because the Witch had decided not to kill her
Because the work kept her from thinking of Kansas
Because the Winkies had promised to help her
Because she hoped to earn the Witch's trust

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch give up harnessing the Lion?
options: He roared and bounded at her so fiercely she was afraid
The gate proved too heavy for her to open
The Winkies refused to hold him for her
She found a horse that suited her better

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does imprisoned describe about the Lion?
options: Shut up and unable to get out
Tied with coils of rope
Kept without any food
Guarded by the Winged Monkeys

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Two prisoners hold out, each helped in secret by the other
A Lion gives in and agrees to draw the chariot
Dorothy escapes the castle by night with Toto
The Winkies rise against the Witch and free them
